subsystems.name: Impoundment wall
subsystems.role: encloses a large volume of sea so it fills and empties through the turbines twice a day.

subsystems.name: Turbine plant
subsystems.role: converts the low head (typically a few metres) into electricity on both ebb and flood.

subsystems.name: Sluice gates
subsystems.role: let water in or out faster than the turbines alone, so the lagoon fills and empties on schedule.

subsystems.name: Sealing and foundations
subsystems.role: stops water short-circuiting under or around the wall, which would waste the impounded head.
parts: cut-off wall to bedrock or low-permeability strata

subsystems.name: Grid connection
subsystems.role: delivers a highly predictable output profile to the coastal network.

subsystems.name: Environmental systems
subsystems.role: manage fish passage, sediment movement and ecology across the wall.

buildSteps.title: Select the bay
buildSteps.detail: Engineers look for a large tidal range, a shallow enclosed area with a narrow mouth, and ground that will hold a seal. Tidal range and impounded area set the energy yield; the shape of the bay must not resonate badly with the tide.

buildSteps.title: Model the hydrodynamics
buildSteps.detail: Numerical models simulate filling and emptying over decades of tides, sizing the turbine and sluice capacity and predicting how the scheme shifts water levels and sediment in the wider estuary.

buildSteps.title: Survey and consent
buildSteps.detail: Geotechnical boreholes find the depth to rock; ecological surveys run for years because the wall changes intertidal habitat and fish routes, and consent is usually the longest step.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the seabed
buildSteps.detail: Dredging levels the foundation line and a cut-off is installed into the seabed so the impounded water cannot leak beneath the wall.

buildSteps.title: Place caissons
buildSteps.detail: Precast concrete caissons with turbine and sluice openings are floated in and ballasted down onto the prepared bed, or a rockfill embankment is built out from the shore with barges.

buildSteps.title: Close the wall
buildSteps.detail: The final gap is closed, turning the bay into a lagoon; this is the highest-risk operation because tidal flow through the narrowing gap accelerates strongly.

buildSteps.title: Install and commission plant
buildSteps.detail: Turbines, generators and gates are installed in the caissons and tested dry, then under water, before the lagoon is first filled through the sluices.

buildSteps.title: Connect and operate
buildSteps.detail: Export cables and the substation are energised, and operating rules are tuned — generating on ebb only, on both tides, or pumping at high tide to raise the head.

prerequisites.why: proven for decades in tidal barrages such as La Rance in France and Sihwa in South Korea; the same machines suit a lagoon.
tides are predictable decades ahead, so output can be scheduled and the environmental effects modelled in advance.
the wall is built from floated-in concrete structures and seabed preparation borrowed from port and bridge engineering.
fish passage and sediment management across a full tidal closure have not yet been demonstrated at lagoon scale, though barrage operators have decades of monitoring.

pathway.milestone: no tidal lagoon operates anywhere; proposals have repeatedly stalled on cost and environmental consent
pathway.unlocks: the engineering is assembled from proven barrage and marine-construction practice.

pathway.milestone: one consented, full-scale lagoon of a few hundred megawatts built and operated through several years of tidal cycles
pathway.unlocks: real capital and operating cost data, and measured ecological effects.

pathway.milestone: two or more lagoons on the same coast with staggered tides
pathway.unlocks: more continuous output, since a lagoon generates on a shifting timetable through the day.

pathway.milestone: lagoons designed jointly as flood defence and generation assets
pathway.unlocks: shared cost with coastal protection and possible pairing with pumped storage or hydrogen.
